chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife before consummating the marriage. He said: 'Upon him is half the dowry, if he had specified for her something; and if he had not specified for her something, then he should provide her with provision in the manner in which similar women are provided with provision.'
By their own selves [i.e., the women themselves], four months and ten days. This is general for all wives, so their ruling must be equal; and also, for he has narrated.

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: consummated the marriage / entered with her
key_terms.لْيُمَتِّعْهَا: he should provide her with provision/maintenance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dowry and maintenance if a man divorces his wife before consummation?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the pre-consummation divorce ruling, distinguishing between cases with a specified dowry (half paid) and those without (mut'ah provided). The text emphasizes the universality of this ruling for all wives, linking the maintenance period to the standard waiting period (iddah) of four months and ten days, a key detail in Shia jurisprudence for determining financial liability before physical intimacy.
